correctness.rationale: Each displayed prime-power formula is exact. The half exponent b=2^(t-1) is even for t>=2, so both factors of the second bi-unitary divisor sum have q+1 and its square divides the sum. Divisibility plus prime support eliminates q=2 and p=2; if both primes are odd, p²+1 has a factor q forcing q≡1 mod4, while ((q+1)/2)²|p² forces q=2p−1, then q|5 forces (p,q)=(3,5). The factor 5^(b+1)+1 has v2=1, must divide 2^(t+1)3², hence ≤18, contrary to ≥126. No finite experiment is treated as infinite proof.

value.rationale: Bi-unitary harmonic perfect squares are exceptionally sparse: the foundational source exhibits a four-prime-square example. The theorem excludes every two-prime square with first exponent exactly two and second exponent any power of two at least four, an infinite and arithmetically natural family. It leverages multiplicity of a q+1 cyclotomic divisor and prime-support forcing, yielding a genuine uniform obstruction beyond finite small-parameter checks and neighboring previously covered families.
